summary: David Kerman Tomlinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019), having also studied under Jay L. Garfield and Andrew Rotman, and held a post at Smith College.
David Kopf (1930–2023) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1960–1965) and served on the faculty at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1997.
David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and was affiliated with the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1987–1989) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1989; Professor Emeritus attested 2026).

David L. McMahan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He previously taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, and held positions at Franklin & Marshall College, including as Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013).

David Ludden is an Indologist and historian. Educated at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania, he taught at the University of Virginia, the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and New York University, where he became Professor of Political Economy and Globalization in 2007.

David M. DiValerio is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the SIT Graduate Institute and the University of Virginia (PhD attested 2011) under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, among other teachers, he held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2015).

David M. Knipe is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor from 1975, Chair of Religious Studies in 1989, and ultimately Professor Emeritus (attested 2026).

David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004, 2013) and as President Emeritus of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian of religion. After studies at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under A. L. Basham, he held a long-term post at El Colegio de México (1970–2010), becoming emeritus in 2019.

David Ownby is a historian, sinologist, and scholar of religion who earned his PhD from Harvard (~1982–1989). He taught at Southern Methodist University (~1991–1993) and served as Professor of History at the University of Montreal (1994–2023).

David P. Jackson is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. He served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Geshe Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Pingree (1933–2005) was an Indologist and historian of science. Educated at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer, he was a professor at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) and Brown University from 1971.

David Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and East Asian religions. After earning his PhD at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, he became an associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).

David R. Kinsley (1939–2000) was an Indologist and scholar of religion. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, and spent his career on the faculty at McMaster University (1969–2000).

David R. Loy is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the National University of Singapore. He taught at NUS (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey (1917–2005) was a classicist and Tibetologist educated at Cambridge. He held fellowships and lectureships at Cambridge, taught at the University of Michigan, and served as Pope Professor of Latin at Harvard University (1975–1988).
David Ruddell (1943–2015) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He was educated at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard (~1990–1996) after studying at Stanford. He has spent his career at UCLA, where he joined the faculty in 1996, served as dean of Humanities (2012), and became Professor (2020).
